ar_haunted_wall.blurb: Haunted Wall is the standout face at Haunt Hollow, a small crag in the Cowell and Deer area of north-central Arkansas. Around 14 climbs line a continuous, steeply overhanging wall roughly 60 feet tall, nearly all of them bolted, plus a couple of easier lines. The grades lean hard: a few climbs from 5.7 to 5.9, three 5.10s, a pair of 5.11s, then a strong block of 5.12s and a single 5.14 at the very top. The wall faces south to southeast and catches plenty of sun. Expect sustained, pumpy climbing rather than a beginner crag.

yt_mcintyre_bluffs.blurb: McIntyre Bluffs is a small, quiet cluster of short cliffs along Fish Lake Road, a few minutes' drive north of Whitehorse in the Yukon. The 15 climbs are mostly traditional, with a few bolted lines and some top-rope options. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.11, with the largest group sitting at 5.10, so it suits climbers who are comfortable placing their own gear on moderate to stiff grades. The setting is peaceful and noticeably less busy than other climbing close to town, and it makes an easy short outing from the city.

yt_zen_garden.blurb: Zen Garden is a limestone crag on the Mount White side of the Alaska Highway, east of Whitehorse in the Yukon. It lies very close to the road, with a short stroll in from a big parking circle. The 15 routes mix sport lines, trad climbs and one top-rope problem. Grades start at an easy 5.5 and reach 5.13, though most routes fall in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, which makes it most useful for intermediate and strong climbers. The quick access makes it a handy place for a short session.

ar_warm_up_boulder.blurb: Warm-Up Boulder is one of ten boulder groupings in the Idaho Boulders at Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas. It is an early stop on foot from the ranch buildings, just downhill from a neighbouring boulder, and it lives up to its name: several of its 14 problems are V0 or V1, which makes it a friendly place to loosen up. Above that the grades spread widely, with a few mid-range problems from V3 to V6 and a small top end reaching V9 and V10. Boulders in this area sit close together, so moving on is easy, though it can get busy.

ar_main_wall_3.blurb: Main Wall is one of five walls at Piney Bowl, a sport crag in the Big Piney region of north-central Arkansas. All 14 routes are bolted, and the wall sits to the left of the waterfall, just before the drop down to the neighbouring FMO Wall. It is a wall for stronger climbers: one route at 5.10, five at 5.11, a large group of 5.12s and a single 5.13. Star ratings are mostly three to four, so the lines are well regarded. Getting to the bowl takes some effort on rough roads or a steep trail.

ar_nowlin_creek.blurb: Nowlin Creek is a newer climbing area at Rattlesnake Ridge Natural Area, in the River Valley and Ouachitas region of Arkansas near Roland. Of its 14 climbs, 13 are sport routes and one is a V3 boulder problem. The routes are gentle by most standards, running from 5.7 to 5.9 with the majority at 5.8, which makes the crag a good pick for newer leaders and anyone building mileage. A short walk from the parking lot reaches the base.
ar_nowlin_creek.approach: Follow the signed trail due west from the parking lot to the crag.
